answer_text: A prime number greater than 1 has only 1 and itself as positive divisors, unlike a composite number such as 8, which also divides evenly by 2 and 4; 2 is the sole even prime since every other even number is divisible by 2, examples include 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, and primality can be checked by testing divisors up to the square root — a property RSA encryption relies on via the difficulty of factoring two large primes.
